newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares recover on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares recover on foreign buying.

text.p: Slovenian shares rose 2.19 percent on Tuesday on the back of buying from foreign investors and traders said they expected the market to continue rising in the short-term.
"The mood on the market is rather optimstic and I think we can expect the formation of a positive trend," Alain Al Soufi, a trader at brokers BPH said.
The 10-share SBI index rose 25.36 points, recovering from Monday's 2.46 percent decline which was blamed on a technical correction.
"Foreign investors were mostly buying shares of newly privatised companies like Lek, Kolinska and Terme Catez and domestic investors might join them in a while," Al Soufi added.
Turnover jumped to 141.9 million tolars from 25.1 million. Overall nine shares rose, four fell, while 12 were untraded. Traders said volumes were likely continue rising as the index advanced.
Drug maker Lek's issue A was the most actively traded share, firming 3.57 percent to 20,300 tolars on volume of 3,269 shares for total turnover of 65.4 million tolars.
Food producer Kolinska was the biggest gainer, rising 5.46 percent to 1,951 tolars on volume of 2,918 shares.
Brokerage Dadas was the leading decliner, falling 4.62 percent to 6,200 on volume of 68 shares.
Elsewhere, health resort Terme Catez rose 3.73 percent or 410 tolars to 11,410 tolars on volume of 398 shares.
